A Trautmann Middle School student is channeling his positive energy into an entrepreneurial venture, according to KGNS. Adrian Cazares, widely known to his school community as "Chief," has launched his own sunglasses brand, "Chief 21."

The middle schooler is known on campus for high-fiving classmates, competing in athletics, and earning a spot on the homecoming court. Trautmann Principal Andrea Garza described him as colorful and full of life, and said he is highly involved and very much loved by students.

The idea began when Cazares and his older brother, Gael, began wearing oversized athletic sunglasses. Cazares embraced the look, and that prompted the idea to start the business. The name combines his nickname with 21, the chromosome associated with Down syndrome, making the brand a statement of Down syndrome awareness. Trautmann special education teacher America De Leon praised the logo and its meaning.

The nickname itself traces back to his childhood, when his father called him "Chivo" because his cries resembled a baby goat. Later, a classmate misheard the Spanish word as "Chief," and the name stuck.

Cazares and his family regularly set up at weekend pop-up markets and are working on launching a website for the brand. His family views the business as a long-term endeavor that can grow with him into high school, college, and beyond, according to his sister, Adriana Rodriguez. In recognition of National Down Syndrome Awareness Month, the city also recognized Cazares this month for his entrepreneurial work.
